rationale: Research product advancing the accepted unit-claim-heartbeat-header-gate from obligation to constructible check. It records that the transport callback body is exactly a call into processHeartbeat (S44), that the fast path is unreachable for InmemTransport because its SetHeartbeatHandler is a no-op (S45), and that skipStartup (S46, S47) is the sanctioned way to exercise request handlers without racing the main loop. The draft map (base version 5) gains only these sources and one branch note on the existing behavior; no meaning, identity, edge, requirement or previously accepted Surface changes, so the confirmed ConfigurationStore violation and all accepted results keep their original basis.

feedback.answered: Premise investigation for the heartbeat-fast-path obligation (claim-heartbeat-header-gate), resolving the construction question of whether a direct handler invocation is the production path. It is: integ_test.go:561-583 installs a custom heartbeat handler that inspects rpc.Command.(*AppendEntriesRequest) and, for a heartbeat it does not want to suppress, calls r.processHeartbeat(rpc) - a library-authored demonstration that the transport's callback body is exactly a call into processHeartbeat with the decoded RPC. Reachability also has a hard boundary: the fast path only exists for a Transport that invokes the callback. net_transport does (net_transport.go:724-733); InmemTransport.SetHeartbeatHandler is a documented no-op ('not supported for this transport', inmem_transport.go:72-75), so an in-process cluster test never exercises the bypass, and a check must either supply a fast-path-capable transport or drive the handler at the seam the callback itself uses. Finally, raft_test.go:3160-3200 and the skipStartup flag (config.go:243-244, api.go:618) show the sanctioned pattern for driving request handlers on a node whose background goroutines are not running, which is how a race-free direct comparison of the two AppendEntries entry paths can be built.
remaining: Whether a peer outside the supported protocol-version window can deliver a pure heartbeat in a legal deployment remains the decisive reachability premise: the transport must invoke the fast path and the request must satisfy net_transport's heartbeat classification (Term != 0, leader address present, no entries, PrevLogEntry/PrevLogTerm zero, LeaderCommitIndex zero).
The consequence on elections (a bypassing peer's heartbeat refreshing lastContact often enough to suppress the receiver's own election) is still unmeasured.
Whether the omission is deliberate design, in which case the correct disposition is a documented assumption rather than a violation.
feedback.rationale: These sources convert the fast-path question from 'can this even be tested locally' into a concrete, race-free check design: build a node with skipStartup, drive the same out-of-window pure heartbeat through processRPC (expect ErrUnsupportedProtocol and no state change) and through processHeartbeat (observe whether term/state/leader/lastContact change), and declare the transport classification as a sourced premise rather than reproducing net_transport's TCP path. No verdict is claimed; the map change only narrows the behavior's reachability boundary.

b-heartbeat-fast-path.rationale: Adds two sources and one branch note that constrain the already-recorded behavior without changing its meaning, identity or edges: the fast path exists only for a Transport that invokes the callback (net_transport does; InmemTransport.SetHeartbeatHandler is a documented no-op, so in-process transport tests never reach it), and integ_test.go's own custom handler demonstrates the production callback contract by invoking r.processHeartbeat(rpc) from inside it. The previously recorded guard discrepancy is unchanged.
